derivation_notes: The fixed-environment assumption is relaxed by allowing the effective recombination intensity to evolve toward a nonnegative setpoint on its own timescale, representing transient mating or chromosomal pairing conditions during the observation window. The initial condition for recombination_rate is chosen away from its setpoint so the added state is dynamically active rather than trapped on the zero-effect manifold where the parent law is recovered exactly.
change_summary: The LD decay law remains proportional to the instantaneous recombination intensity, but that intensity is no longer fixed and instead relaxes dynamically toward a setpoint. This creates time-varying proportional erosion of D and therefore curvature in log|D| versus time.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: The recombination intensity is constant through time.
assumption_audit.mechanism: Temporal relaxation of effective recombination intensity due to changing mating or chromosomal pairing conditions, while recombination still always erodes LD toward zero.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: The successor reduces to the parent when recombination_rate is constant in time, equivalently if recombination_relaxation_rate=0 or if the initial recombination_rate equals recombination_setpoint.

response_change.parent_relation: With a constant recombination_rate, the target mapping is dD_dt versus D as a single linear decay with one shared slope: dD_dt=-recombination_rate*D.
response_change.child_relation: Release recombination intensity from being time-constant by allowing it to relax as a state, so the target mapping becomes dD_dt=-r(t)*D with time-varying slope magnitude during the trajectory.
response_change.observable_effect: Across trajectories observed over time with the same initial D, the parent predicts a straight line in dD_dt versus D with fixed proportionality, whereas the child predicts changing proportionality over time, visible as non-exponential decay of |D| and curvature on a semilog plot.

evolution_contract.activation_condition: Observable when recombination environment changes on comparable timescales to LD decay, so the effective recombination intensity is not approximately constant over the observation window; if recombination relaxes much faster or much slower than D, the parent may be an adequate approximation.
evolution_contract.train_hidden_contrast: In training, mild departure from a pure exponential decay appears as time-varying proportional loss of D; in holdout, stronger or longer observations reveal clearer semilog curvature from the same mechanism.
evolution_contract.continuation_path: Recover the parent when the recombination state is constant in time, equivalently when its relaxation rate is zero or its initial value equals its steady value for all t.
evolution_contract.promotion_reason: A time-varying recombination intensity cannot be represented with the existing single fixed parameter if one must use one shared parameter set across trajectories; it needs its own ODE state to encode environmental relaxation during the experiment.
evolution_contract.scientific_mechanism: Temporal relaxation of effective recombination intensity due to changing mating or chromosomal pairing conditions, while recombination still always erodes LD toward zero.
evolution_contract.difficulty_rationale: This embedding introduces a distinct recombination-relaxation timescale that directly modulates the scored D dynamics, producing non-exponential decay and a time-varying proportional loss rate rather than a coefficient-only rescaling of one fixed exponential.
evolution_contract.assumption_before: The recombination intensity is constant through time.
evolution_contract.assumption_after: The effective recombination intensity is an internal state that relaxes toward a setpoint during the experiment.
evolution_contract.parent_reduction: The successor reduces to the parent when recombination_relaxation_rate=0 or when the initial recombination_rate equals recombination_setpoint, making recombination_rate constant for all t.
evolution_contract.observable_signature: With the same initial D and one shared parameter set, the parent gives a single exponential D(t) and constant dD_dt/D, while the child gives time-varying dD_dt/D and curvature in log|D| versus t whenever recombination_rate starts away from recombination_setpoint and relaxes on a comparable timescale.
evolution_contract.shortcut_blocked: A single refitted constant parent recombination_rate can match only one effective proportional decay slope, not the within-trajectory drift in dD_dt/D generated when recombination_rate itself relaxes over time. Across observation windows where that relaxation is visible, one shared parent parameter set cannot reproduce both early-time and late-time decay behavior.

Vary the observation time window and trajectories in which effective recombination conditions relax, while holding neutrality, fixed marginal allele frequencies, and absence of mutation/migration/drift/selection unchanged. The parent enforces one exponential decay shape for D(t) with a single constant proportional slope for all times. The child allows that proportional slope to change during the run as recombination_rate evolves, producing curvature in log|D| versus t and a non-constant dD_dt/D. This is a changed target mapping, not merely auxiliary complexity, because the scored derivative of D directly depends on the evolving recombination_rate. The effect is admissible so long as recombination_rate remains nonnegative, ensuring dD_dt always points toward zero and D=0 stays invariant. Limitation: if the effective recombination intensity is nearly constant over the sampled interval, the refinement will not be distinguishable from the parent.

derivation_notes: The parent assumes a fixed proportional erosion law across the full admissible LD range. Here an internal occupancy-limitation state is added so finite haplotype occupancy can compete with recombination; the chosen nonzero initial condition avoids starting exactly on the zero-effect branch while remaining scientifically small and nonnegative.
change_summary: The strictly linear decay law was refined to include state-dependent saturation of recombination-driven erosion at larger |D|. This changes the scored mapping from D to dD_dt because the normalized decay gain now decreases when occupancy limitation accumulates.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: The loss of association is exactly proportional to D over the full admissible range.
assumption_audit.mechanism: Finite-haplotype occupancy can limit the amount of association effectively available to be broken down, so recombination competes with an internal saturation process at high |D|.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: The parent is recovered when occupancy_buffer stays near 0, for example in the weak-association limit D≈0 or when occupancy_sensitivity->0 so the added state remains inactive.

response_change.parent_relation: The target mapping is dD_dt = -recombination_rate*D, so for any observed recombination_rate the decay magnitude is a single linear gain in |D| with constant local slope -recombination_rate.
response_change.child_relation: Replace the strictly linear erosion law with a bounded odd dependence on D so the effective decay gain decreases as |D| approaches its admissible maximum, while retaining the sign toward zero. Then dD_dt remains zero at D=0 and opposite in sign to D, but the |D|->|dD_dt| relation becomes curved rather than purely linear.
response_change.observable_effect: At fixed observed recombination_rate, small |D| still decays approximately exponentially, but larger |D| decays more slowly than the linear parent predicts, producing state-dependent curvature in D(t) and a smaller-than-linear magnitude of dD_dt at high |D|.

evolution_contract.activation_condition: Observable when trajectories sample a non-negligible range of |D|, especially moderate-to-large |D| relative to its feasible scale; effect is weak near D=0 where the child must reduce to the parent approximately.
evolution_contract.train_hidden_contrast: In training, modest |D| already shows near-zero versus moderate-|D| differences in effective decay gain; in holdout, larger |D| extends this same curvature, with stronger attenuation of decay magnitude than any single linear gain can match across all sampled states.
evolution_contract.continuation_path: Recover the parent law in the weak-association limit where |D| is small compared with its saturation scale, so the nonlinear erosion factor linearizes to 1.
evolution_contract.promotion_reason: A saturation scale is needed to express when finite feasible haplotype constraints begin to blunt the proportional erosion of LD. Existing symbols provide only D and a time-varying recombination_rate, which cannot by themselves encode a separate internal measure of available recombinantizable association without collapsing back to a refit linear gain.
evolution_contract.domain_mechanism: competition between recombination-driven LD erosion and finite-occupancy limitation
evolution_contract.scientific_mechanism: Finite-haplotype occupancy can limit the amount of association that is effectively available to be broken down, making recombination-driven erosion saturate at large |D| even though it still points toward linkage equilibrium.
evolution_contract.difficulty_rationale: The added internal state creates a history-dependent attenuation of the decay gain, so the same observed recombination_rate can produce different dD_dt values depending on accumulated occupancy limitation. This is structurally harder than a coefficient-only correction because the target map is no longer a single line in D with one shared gain.
evolution_contract.assumption_before: The loss of association is exactly proportional to D over the full admissible range.
evolution_contract.assumption_after: Finite-haplotype occupancy builds an internal limitation state that competes with recombination and reduces effective erosion at larger |D|.
evolution_contract.parent_reduction: The parent is recovered when occupancy_sensitivity->0 or occupancy_relaxation_rate is fast while D remains small enough that occupancy_buffer≈0.
evolution_contract.observable_signature: Vary the observed state D along trajectories while holding the recombination-rate relaxation parameters fixed. In the parent, once recombination_rate is given, the target mapping from D to dD_dt is a single straight line through the origin with slope -recombination_rate. In the child, two times with the same observed recombination_rate but different |D| can have different normalized decay gains because occupancy limitation suppresses erosion, so larger |D| shows smaller-than-linear |dD_dt|. This target-mapping contrast is observable when trajectories include moderate-to-large |D| under the stated initial-condition contract; near D=0 the refinement becomes hard to distinguish and approximately recovers the parent.
evolution_contract.shortcut_blocked: A single refitted parent parameter set cannot reproduce both the near-origin slope and the attenuated large-|D| decay across one dataset spanning those conditions, because its D-to-dD_dt map remains exactly linear for all D once recombination_rate is specified. Changing only the auxiliary recombination_rate trajectory is insufficient because the scored contrast compares observations with the same recombination_rate but different occupancy-driven attenuation.

derivation_notes: The exact proportionality of recombination-driven LD loss to D is relaxed by introducing an odd cubic correction in the same recombination process, so larger |D| erodes faster while D=0 remains invariant. This keeps the original occupancy moderation but changes the target mapping itself rather than only auxiliary trajectories.
change_summary: The successor replaces strictly linear LD erosion with amplitude-dependent nonlinear erosion under the same recombination and occupancy buffering mechanism. Small |D| remains approximately parent-like, while moderate |D| decays faster at fixed recombination_rate and occupancy_buffer.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: The loss of association is proportional to the association currently available to be broken down.
assumption_audit.mechanism: At stronger disequilibrium, the excess of overrepresented haplotypes can make recombinant generation of counterbalancing haplotypes scale more than linearly with association amplitude while still relaxing toward linkage equilibrium.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: Setting nonlinear_ld_coupling = 0 recovers the parent expression exactly.

response_change.parent_relation: For fixed recombination_rate and occupancy_buffer, the target mapping is linear in D: dD_dt = -(recombination_rate/(1+occupancy_buffer))*D, so the erosion strength per unit |D| is independent of |D| once the auxiliary states are given.
response_change.child_relation: Replace the strictly linear dependence on D by a steeper odd restoring law whose effective erosion per unit |D| increases with |D| while preserving the sign toward zero, e.g. a nonlinear dependence on D within the recombination term moderated by the same occupancy factor.
response_change.observable_effect: At matched recombination_rate and occupancy_buffer, small |D| decays nearly as before but larger |D| decays disproportionately faster, producing a curved relationship between |D| and |dD_dt| that the parent's single gain cannot match over both weak- and strong-LD portions of the same trajectory.

derivation_notes: The one-phase occupancy limitation is relaxed by introducing a slower refractory occupancy-memory state that accumulates from D**2 and decays on its own timescale. Its effect on D erosion is saturating, representing finite-capacity crowding or access limitation, and the chosen nonzero initial condition keeps the branch scientifically active without closing it on an invariant zero-effect set.
change_summary: The successor adds a slow refractory occupancy memory that continues to suppress recombinational erosion after sustained high-|D| exposure. This changes the target mapping by making dD_dt depend on recent LD history through a saturating hidden state, not only on the current D and fast occupancy buffer.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: Occupancy limitation is fully captured by one fast linear relaxation variable slaved to current D**2, with no slower refractory or crowding-memory phase.
assumption_audit.mechanism: Sustained excess occupancy of overrepresented haplotypes can leave a slower refractory crowding state that continues to limit effective recombinant reshuffling even after instantaneous LD has already begun to relax, while still preserving decay toward D=0.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: The successor reduces to the parent when refractory_occupancy_strength = 0, or when refractory_occupancy_relaxation_rate is infinitely fast together with negligible refractory_occupancy_sensitivity so the added memory contributes no sustained suppression.

response_change.parent_relation: For fixed recombination_rate and occupancy_buffer, dD_dt is an odd monotone function of D whose magnitude changes with |D| only through a single rational dependence on D**2, so positive and negative associations with the same |D| decay with the same one-phase shape.
response_change.child_relation: Retain decay toward zero but relax the assumption that the occupancy limitation responds instantaneously with one linear relaxation mode; introduce a slowly accumulating refractory occupancy memory so the effective erosion at a given current |D| depends on recent prior |D| exposure, changing the local curvature of the D-to-dD_dt mapping during sustained large-|D| episodes versus transient ones.
response_change.observable_effect: Two trajectories that pass through the same current D can show different |dD_dt| depending on whether they arrived after prolonged high |D| or after a brief excursion; sustained high |D| yields stronger temporary suppression of erosion than the parent can produce from current D alone.
